queenstown-crown-range-and-milford-appro.title: Queenstown · Crown Range and Milford Approach
queenstown-crown-range-and-milford-appro.slogan: Alpine lake roads and a weather-aware overnight plan.
queenstown-crown-range-and-milford-appro.story: Alpine lake roads and a weather-aware overnight plan. Out of Arrowtown and back again: 356 km, roughly 6 h 51 in the saddle. It goes by way of Wanaka lake stop, Milford Road high section and Te Anau overnight. Crown Range Road is the high point. It tops out at about 1,150 m. The passes are the reason to go.
queenstown-crown-range-and-milford-appro.hero: Queenstown · Crown Range and Milford Approach

sections.advice: Use Wanaka lake stop → Milford Road high section as clean positioning. Keep it tidy, ignore impatient traffic and save the enthusiasm for the good road ahead. The value here is not drama; it is arriving at the riding section with space, fuel and concentration intact.

sections.advice: This Te Anau overnight → Back to Crown Range Road stretch is for rhythm and scenery. Keep your head up, let the view breathe, and resist turning every open bend into a target. Stop once properly rather than half-stopping everywhere.

scenicChapters.title: Crown Range Road
scenicChapters.narrative: Slow enough to look. The surface follows the shoreline, so the corners arrive where the water decided, not where an engineer did. Water arrives beside the road and stays for 46 km. The line follows the shore because there is nowhere else for it to go.

scenicChapters.title: Segment San Juan de Tantaranche - Huarochi → Segment Casila Alto - Chi
scenicChapters.narrative: Slow enough to look. The surface follows the shoreline, so the corners arrive where the water decided, not where an engineer did. Water arrives beside the road and stays for 45 km. The line follows the shore because there is nowhere else for it to go.

places-segment-masho-piticocha-segment-s.story: A 212 km round trip from Tanta - roughly 3 h 39 in the saddle. It goes by way of Segment San Juan de Tantaranche - Huarochi, Segment Casila Alto - Chillaco, Segment Sisicaya - Santa Rosa de Chontay and back through Segment Casila Alto - Chillaco. The highest point is about 4,700 m. The line favours views over speed.
